'''Tie:''' {{legend0|#cdafdc|40–50%}} | title = U.S. Senator | before_election = [[Byron Dorgan]] | before_party = North Dakota Democratic-NPL Party | after_election = [[Byron Dorgan]] | after_party = North Dakota Democratic-NPL Party }} {{ElectionsND}} The '''1998 United States Senate election in North Dakota''' was held on November 3, 1998, along with other elections to the [[United States Senate]] as well as elections to the [[United States House of Representatives]] and various state and local elections. Incumbent [[North Dakota Democratic-NPL Party|Democratic-NPL]] U.S. Senator [[Byron Dorgan]] won re-election to a second term.{{cite web|url=http://clerk.house.gov/members/electionInfo/1998/98Stat.htm#34 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20040416012700/http://clerk.house.gov/members/electionInfo/1998/98Stat.htm |archivedate=April 16, 2004|title=Statistics of the Congressional Election of November 3, 1998}} == Major candidates == === Democratic === * [[Byron Dorgan]], incumbent U.S. Senator === Republican === * [[Donna Nalewaja]], [[North Dakota Senate|State Senator]] == Campaign == Nalewaja's campaign focused on the suggestion that Dorgan had served in the [[United States Congress]] for nearly 20 years, and had accomplished relatively little. Dorgan and Nalewaja won the primary elections for their respective parties. McLain had previously run for this Senate seat in [[1980 United States Senate election in North Dakota|1980]] against eventual winner [[Mark Andrews (politician)|Mark Andrews]] and [[Kent Johanssen]] for the open seat given up by retiring Senator [[Milton Young]]. == Results == {{Election box begin no change | title = 1998 United States Senate election, North Dakota}} {{Election box winning candidate with party link no change | party = North Dakota Democratic-NPL Party | candidate = [[Byron Dorgan]] (incumbent) | votes = 134,747 | percentage = 63.16% }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change | party = Republican Party (United States) | candidate = [[Donna Nalewaja]] | votes = 75,013 | percentage = 35.16% }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change | party = Reform Party of the United States of America | candidate = Harley McLain | votes = 3,598 | percentage = 1.69% }} {{Election box total no change | votes = 213,358 | percentage = 100.00% }} {{Election box hold with party link without swing | winner = North Dakota Democratic-NPL Party | loser = | swing = }} {{Election box end}} == See also == * [[1998 United States Senate elections]] == References == {{Reflist}} == External links == * [https://web.archive.org/web/20080823134337/http://web.apps.state.nd.us/sec/emspublic/gp/electionresultssearch.htm?cmd=Search&searchType=STATE&electionDate=11031998&showMap=N 1998 North Dakota U.S. Senate Election results] {{United States elections, 1998}} {{NDUSSenateElections}} [[Category:1998 United States Senate elections|North Dakota]] [[Category:United States Senate elections in North Dakota|1998]] [[Category:1998 elections in North Dakota|United States Senate]]
